readout_other: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recorded from a surface electrode over the C2 barrel column (S1BF); peak amplitude, peak latency, and power spectral density (alpha/beta band) analysis
direction_notes: Ultrasound preceding whisker stimulation by 25 ms significantly enhanced subsequent whisker-evoked cortical response amplitude and alpha/beta power (facilitation), whereas whisker stimulation preceding ultrasound by 10 ms significantly suppressed the ultrasound-evoked response; no facilitation/suppression was seen at 100 ms, indicating a temporally specific bidirectional excitability window.

exposures.label: Ultrasound stimulation of C2 barrel column (frequency and whisker-timing paradigm)

target.label: C2 barrel column, primary somatosensory cortex (S1BF)

timing.protocol_description: A craniotomy was performed and the skull removed so that ultrasound was delivered directly onto the exposed dura via coupling gel. Three ultrasound frequencies (1, 2, 4 MHz) were tested in each animal with intensity and PRF held constant. Ultrasound was combined with whisker stimulation in whisker-ultrasound (W-U) and ultrasound-whisker (U-W) sequences at inter-stimulus intervals of 10, 25, and 100 ms. Each stimulation session lasted 2 s, with 100 continuous stimulations per condition, a 3-min inter-sequence interval, and a 1-h rest between different ultrasound frequencies in the same animal.

source_quotes.n_subjects: This study used 30 adult male Sprague–Dawley (SD) healthy rats, weighing 250–350g.
source_quotes.exposures[0].target.label: This placement targeted the center of the C2 barrel column within the primary somatosensory cortex (S1BF).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: We designed a temporally shifted sensory paradigm to test how ultrasound frequency (1, 2, and 4 MHz), inter-stimulus interval (10, 25, and 100 ms), and stimulation order (ultrasound–whisker vs. whisker–ultrasound) affect cortical responses in the rat barrel cortex.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: The ultrasound system used in this study included a HIFU ultrasound transducer, manufactured by Siansonic Inc., Xi'an, China.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: In compliance with regulatory safety thresholds, the ultrasonic neuromodulation protocol employed a spatial-peak temporal-average intensity $( I _ { \mathrm { s p t a } } )$ of 700mW/ cm<sup>2</sup>, approximately 97% of the FDA-mandated diagnostic ultrasound limit (720mW/cm<sup>2</sup>).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: During the experiment, we kept the ultrasound stimulation intensity and pulse repetition frequency (500 Hz) constant to ensure uniform ultrasound intensity across all experimental conditions. Each ultrasound pulse had a duration of 100 μs to maintain consistency in the stimulation.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: During the experiment, we kept the ultrasound stimulation intensity and pulse repetition frequency (500 Hz) constant to ensure uniform ultrasound intensity across all experimental conditions. Each ultrasound pulse had a duration of 100 μs to maintain consistency in the stimulation.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Each stimulation session maintained 2 s, and a total of 100 continuous stimulations were administered to ensure the reproducibility of the experiment.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: To minimize the cumulative neural effects of different ultrasound frequencies within the same rat, a 1-h rest interval was set between stimulations of each frequency.

flags.reason: Each animal underwent a single terminal craniotomy experiment covering all frequency/interval conditions, but the paper does not explicitly state a number of sessions per animal.
Duty cycle not explicitly stated; only PRF (500 Hz) and pulse duration (100 µs) are given, which would allow computation (5%) but this was not done per the no-arithmetic rule.

Domain of the reported Ispta (700 mW/cm2) is not stated as free-field or in-situ; ultrasound is applied directly onto the exposed dura (craniotomy) via gel, with no skull path, but the paper does not label the measurement domain.
No sham/placebo ultrasound condition was used; whisker-only and ultrasound-only conditions served as unimodal reference comparators, not an inactive-device sham.
